ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a benzene ring, and the benzene ring is connected to an organic side chain; in the side chain there is a carbon bearing OH, an adjacent carbon, an HN group, and a carbonyl carbon, and the carbonyl carbon is also connected to R. On the right side is a phosphoric acid/pyrophosphate-like portion, where two phosphorus atoms can be seen connected by a bridging oxygen, and each phosphorus also has two terminal oxygen connections drawn; there are also several reaction arrows in the figure, which need to be ignored. Then reason: count by blocks according to the specified method and do not count bonds involving hydrogen. There are 6 heavy-atom bonds within the benzene ring. The organic side chain outside the benzene ring has another 7 heavy-atom bonds: phenyl-C, C-O, C-C, C-N, N-carbonyl C, carbonyl C=O, carbonyl C-R. The phosphate portion on the right has 6 heavy-atom bonds: the bridging oxygen provides two P-O connections, and the other four are terminal P-O/P=O connections. The total is 6 + 7 + 6 = 19.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Partition the structure into fragments. Count 6 heavy-atom bonds in the benzene ring. Count 7 additional heavy-atom bonds in the organic side chain: phenyl-C, C-O, C-C, C-N, N-carbonyl C, carbonyl C=O, and carbonyl C-R. Count 6 heavy-atom bonds in the phosphate portion on the right: the two P-O connections through the bridging O plus the four terminal P-O/P=O connections shown. Ignore all arrows and do not add any O-H or N-H bond. Sum 6 + 7 + 6 = 19.
